t: #3679 Minimum Discards to Balance Inventory — Sliding Window Greedy
o: Process arrivals left to right; each w-day window may contain at most m kept items of any type. Discard as few arrivals as possible. Example 2: with w=3, m=2, the third consecutive 3 must be dropped → 1. The greedy 'discard the current arrival when its type is saturated' is optimal because past decisions are irrevocable and dropping today's item is always at least as good as having dropped an earlier one.
k: Greedy: when keeping today's arrival would push its type to m+1 within the window, discarding today is optimal (any earlier discard could be swapped for today's).
Maintain per-type counts of KEPT items inside the current window; when an item slides out, decrement only if it was kept.
O(n) with a hash map plus a kept-flag array.

a.i: For each day, recount the last w days' kept items per type to decide the discard. Correct but O(n·w) — acceptable only for small inputs; motivates the sliding-window version.
s: For day i, count occurrences of arrivals[i] among kept items in [i-w+1, i-1].
If the count equals m, mark discarded; otherwise keep.
a.t: O(n·w) — recounts each window from scratch.

a.i: Keep a running count of kept items per type inside the window. On each day: if the incoming type already has m kept items in the window, discard it; otherwise keep and increment. Then, as the oldest day exits the window, decrement its count only if it was kept. Every window constraint is maintained incrementally in O(1) per day.
s: Initialize a hash-map counter and a kept[] array.
For day i: if cnt[arrivals[i]] == m, discard (leave kept[i] false); else keep and cnt[arrivals[i]]++.
If day i-w+1 exists and was kept, decrement cnt for its type.
a.t: O(n) — constant work per arrival (hash-map operations amortized O(1)).
a.sp: O(n) for kept flags plus O(distinct types) for the counter.

w: The exchange argument (dropping today beats having dropped any earlier day) is what interviewers want articulated. Pitfalls: decrementing counts for discarded items that leave the window (track kept[]!), and checking saturation BEFORE incrementing. Follow-up: what if discards could happen retroactively, or windows were defined over kept items only?
